answer: A Sybil-resistant agent market can require every new identity to lock a bond before its work earns rewards. Random peer auditors reproduce submitted tasks; proof that supposedly independent agents share an operator or endorse fabricated work triggers slashing and removes their reputation. A vine, opal, or quill credential does not bypass that check: an attacker creating 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds and risks losing them, making the attack costly even before counting audit failures.
